title: Cloud-Native Architecture Quality Attribute Stack
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Software Architecture
description: Interactive layer diagram of the cloud-native stack (IaaS, containers, Kubernetes, infrastructure as code, application and service mesh) showing which quality attributes each layer supports and which it puts at risk.

educational.topic: Quality attribute contributions and risks of the cloud-native technology stack
learningObjectives: Students will be able to identify at least three quality attribute contributions and one quality attribute risk at each layer of the cloud-native technology stack.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Structured comparison: examine each layer, then trace one attribute across layers
keyQuestions: Which quality attributes does each layer support, and through what mechanism?
Which attribute is put at risk at the most layers?
Where does one layer compensate for a weakness introduced by another?
commonMisconceptions: Adopting Kubernetes makes a system available and scalable by itself (probes, replicas, and capacity still have to be designed).
Each layer only adds benefits (every layer also adds complexity or overhead).
Containers isolate workloads as strongly as virtual machines (they share the host kernel).
assessmentOpportunities: Remove one layer (for example, "the team deploys containers by hand, with no orchestrator") and ask students which supported attributes are lost, which risks disappear, and whether the result is a risk or a non-risk for a stated availability scenario.
